info.title: Toknila daemon API
info.description: Local API of the Toknila daemon. Every /v1 route needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from daemon.json.

get.summary:
The agent slots of every project and the cards waiting for one, as core's schedule computes
them.

delete.summary:
Deletes the chain with its cards, milestones and everything attached to them, and their
journal entries, in one transaction; refused (409) while an agent works on one of its cards,
naming them. Then the ships' checkouts are removed from the repository and the cards' run
files deleted. The repository folder and its `ship/*` branches stay. A cleanup step that
fails is listed in `warnings`; the deletion stands either way.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project id or key, when two projects have a chain of this name

patch.summary:
Sets the chain's review mode, reviewer agent profile and autostart. A ticket that sets its
own review keeps it; a field left out is kept. Turning autostart on starts the chain's ready
cards that have a free slot: it is the owner's act, and the journal records it
(`chain.updated`).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project id or key, when two projects have a chain of this name

post.summary: Clears the places a person put the chain's cards at, so the automatic layout draws them.

The person's click on Release: cuts the chain's release milestone and starts the run in the
background. The answer is the chain with the milestone cut; the steps are read from
`GET /releases/{release}/run`, and the milestone reads released when the last one passes.
Puts a card directly before or after another card; the dependencies around it are rewired.
A person proposes a wildcard card: it waits in Proposed until a person approves or rejects it.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return events with seq greater than this.

patch.summary: Edits a card of the planner's project that has not started.

post.summary: Asks the window to show a card of the planner's project (a `window.show_card` event).
Opens a thread on a card of the planner's project.
Posts a message in a thread of a card of the planner's project.

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Thread number on the card (1, 2, ...) or thread id

post.summary: Posts the next artifact version of a thread; an approved thread reopens.

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Thread number on the card (1, 2, ...) or thread id

post.summary: A new chain in the planner's project. It never starts its cards by itself.
A new card in a chain of the planner's project.
Puts a card directly before or after another; the dependencies around it are rewired.
Makes `to` wait for `from`.

get.summary: One design of the planner's project: its metadata and the path of its file.

The whole plan of the planner's project: chains, cards in order, dependencies, threads, and
the project's designs with the path of each file.

post.summary:
Keeps the planner's next step for its project, replacing the previous one (a
`window.suggest` event). The owner's window shows it with the button of its action; the
planner starts, answers and accepts nothing itself.

Creates a project. A folder (`repo_path`) must be a repository with the base branch; the
refusal names the field.

patch.summary:
Changes project settings. A higher parallel limit starts waiting cards at once; a lower one
never stops a running agent. A new base branch must exist in the project's repository and a
default profile must be in the catalog; the refusal names the field.

post.summary: Hides the project from the sidebar and keeps its data. Refused while its agents work.

Deletes the project: its chains, cards, milestones and everything attached to them, with
their journal entries, in one transaction; refused (409) while any of its agents works. Then
the ships' worktrees are removed from the repository and the cards' run files deleted; with
`trash_folder` the repository folder goes to the system Trash. Nothing else in the repository
is touched: its `ship/*` branches stay. A cleanup step that fails is listed in `warnings` (or
`folder_error`); the deletion stands either way.

get.summary: The project's designs, oldest first, and whether it has a Figma token.

post.summary:
Keeps an uploaded png, jpg, webp or pdf (the raw file as the body, its name in `name`). The
kind comes from the file's bytes; a pdf is kept as one design.

Keeps a Figma frame link as a design. With a token saved the frame is fetched as a png and
kept next to the uploads; without one, or when Figma refuses, the link stays with a hint.

delete.summary: Removes a design and its file.

post.summary: Fetches a Figma design's frame again (after a token was saved, or a fetch failed).

get.summary:
The kept file as it was stored, with its media type. It serves as the thumbnail too: the page
scales it.

put.summary:
Saves the project's Figma personal access token as a file under the data home's `secrets`
folder (readable by its owner only). It is never sent back and never written to a log.

post.summary:
Reads a path on this machine and imports what it holds through the ordinary chain import. A
TOML chain file or a spec folder makes one chain, or fails as a whole with a message that
names the path (and, for a `tasks.md`, the line). A folder of spec folders makes one chain per
spec folder, each on its own, and lists the subfolders it skipped and those that failed. Each
chain keeps the path it was read from as its `source`.

200.description: A folder of spec folders none of which could be imported; see `failed`

201.description: At least one chain was imported

get.summary: Everything in the project that waits on a person, newest first, as core computes it.
Whether the project's planner is running.

requestBody.description: Bytes typed into the planner's terminal, as they are

200.description: Raw terminal output of the planner's newest run, last lines only (ANSI kept). Headers x-toknila-run, x-toknila-offset (of the first byte) and x-toknila-end (after the last; continue the stream from here).

post.summary: The size of the panel that shows the planner's terminal.

204.description: Resized; sizes outside 20x5..500x200 are brought into that range

post.summary:
Starts the project's planner in its repository (Claude Code, read-only, with the planner
tools), or keeps the live one.
Stops the project's planner; one that is not running is fine.

get.summary:
Lists the plans in the project's repository: `specs/*/tasks.md` and `plans/*.toml`, one level
deep and never the whole tree, each with its card count and whether a chain of the project
was imported from it, and whether the repository has a `.specify/` folder. A project without a
repository, or whose folder is gone, has none. Importing one is `import-path` with its `path`.

Lists the ships' worktrees and `ship/*` branches in the project's repository that no live
card owns: what cancelled or deleted cards left behind. Nothing is changed.

post.summary:
Removes what `GET .../strays` lists, looked at again now: stray worktrees first (their
checkouts are discarded), then stray branches, whatever commits they hold. A step that fails
is named in `warnings` and that leftover stays.

get.summary: The planner's standing suggestion for the project (the next step), or `null` when it has none.

post.summary: Brings an archived project back to the sidebar.

Is this folder a git repository with the base branch? The branches come back so a form can
offer them when the base is missing.

get.summary: Is `git` new enough, is `claude` installed, is `gh` logged in; each with a fix hint.

The Toknila version, the `tok` that ships next to the daemon and whether `~/.local/bin/tok`
links to it.

post.summary:
Links `~/.local/bin/tok` to the bundled `tok`. Only the person's home is written, never with
elevated rights.

get.summary: Where the data home, the ships and the profiles folder are on this machine.

parameters.name: needs_human
parameters.description: Only tickets waiting on a person (Proposed, Waiting, Blocked, Review).

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: start, pause, resume, block, unblock, accept, return, reopen, cancel, approve, reject or ask_design

post.summary:
A sign of life from the ticket's agent (a hook fired). Recorded as the run's last activity;
it also ends the run's startup wait and the questions that were open for it. A `PreToolUse`
hook says which tool is about to run, and a permission notification (`prompt`) asks the person
(the worker's card waits, a reviewer's dialog is listed in the inbox).

A person says something to the project's assistant about the card: the message goes in the
card's discussion thread (opened by the first one). The text for the planner's terminal is the
window's to send.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

post.summary:
The ticket's agent asks, from its Stop hook, for what a person told it while it worked. Each
instruction is handed out once: it is marked delivered as it is claimed.
A person's decision about the open subtasks left behind a card done out of order.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: The earlier card that holds the open subtasks (id or key)

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: move (into a new card at the end of the chain), close or leave

post.summary:
The agent's `PermissionRequest` hook: a permission dialog is about to show. The worker's card
waits for the person (a reviewer's dialog is listed in the inbox), and the call is held until
the person allows or denies in the window, up to the daemon's wait; then the agent shows its
own dialog (`decision: ask`).

A person's answer to what the ticket's worker or reviewer asks: allow or deny a permission, or
a key or text for an agent that waits on its screen. Core says which answers the open question
takes; an answer to a permission goes to the agent's waiting hook, else to its terminal. The
card of a waiting worker is Running again at once.

204.description: Delivered to the agent and journaled

requestBody.description: Bytes typed into the agent's terminal, as they are

200.description: Raw terminal output of the newest run of the worker (or, with role=reviewer, of the reviewer), last lines only (ANSI kept). Headers x-toknila-run, x-toknila-offset (of the first byte) and x-toknila-end (after the last; continue the stream from here).

post.summary:
The size of the panel that shows the agent's terminal. The agent is a full-screen terminal
program, so its terminal follows the panel.

204.description: Resized; sizes outside 20x5..500x200 are brought into that range

get.summary: A ticket's threads with their messages and versions, and its phase.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

post.summary: A person opens a thread on a ticket.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

parameters.name: thread

parameters.name: thread

parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Thread number on the ticket (1, 2, ...) or thread id

post.summary: A person posts a new artifact version; an approved thread reopens.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket id or key, e.g. DEMO-3

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Thread number on the ticket (1, 2, ...) or thread id

get.summary:
Tokens and estimated API cost over the last 7, 30 or 90 days: totals, a series per UTC day and
breakdowns by model, project, chain, card and workspace. Costs are estimates at API list
prices; on a subscription the real cost differs.

post.summary:
The plan limits an agent's status line received from Claude Code (`rate_limits`); the page
shows them as the remaining quota until the windows reset.

put.summary: Counts every Claude Code session on this machine (the default), or only Toknila's runs.

ActionInput.description: Body of ticket actions. `text` is required by block, return and cancel.

Actor.description: Who did something: a person, an agent, or the system (graph rules, autostart).

oneOf.description: The runner is up and the agent is working. Starts a Ready ticket; no-op if Running.
The agent needs a person: a question, or permission for an action.

detail.description: The whole command a permission request is about, when `text` is only its summary.

oneOf.description: The agent ticked a checklist item (1-based position).
A short progress report, stored as a report comment.
The agent is done; the summary becomes a report comment and the ticket goes to Review.
The agent process died.

Only the reviewer agent's token may send this: its decision about the diff. The comment
says what to change and is required with `request_changes`.

items.description: PASS or FAIL for each acceptance item of the ticket (required when it has any).

allOf.description:
The agent found work nobody planned: a wildcard card on the ticket's chain, found during
this ticket, that waits for a person's approval. The answer is the new card.

oneOf.description:
The agent found work nobody planned: a wildcard card on the ticket's chain, found during
this ticket, that waits for a person's approval. The answer is the new card.

The agent opens a thread to settle a design, a flow or an architecture with the owner.
The hand-in is refused until every thread is approved.
A message from the agent in a thread (`thread`: its number on this ticket, or its id).
A new artifact version from the agent. A new version reopens an approved thread.

AgentEvent.description: One report from the agent working on a ticket.

AgentProfile.description:
How to launch an agent and in which role. A new agent is a new profile file, not new code.
The working directory is not part of it: the ship supplies it at launch.

command.description:
Program and arguments, never a shell string. Empty only for the simulated profile, which
starts no process: a person sends its events from the CLI.

instructions_file.description: Instructions file the agent reads, relative to its working directory.

instructions_flag.description:
Flag of the agent's command that takes the path of the generated per-run instructions
(under the data home; the project's own instructions file is never written).

startup_secs.description:
Seconds after spawn without any sign of life from the agent (hook or MCP) before the
window shows that it waits on its screen. 0 turns the check off.

AgentRole.description: What an agent profile is for.

AnswerKind.description: One way a person answers a question.

ArtifactFormat.description: How an artifact body is to be read.

oneOf.description: A person blocked it by hand.
The runner process crashed.

The agent's process was ended from outside (terminated or killed by another tool or the
user); `detail` says how. Unblocking starts it again.
A dependency was reopened after it had merged.
Merging into the base branch conflicted; `detail` names the files.

The base branch is checked out with local changes, so the merge would have to touch the
person's files. Nothing was changed.

The merge could not run or finish (the VCS is missing or too old, a branch is gone, the
base kept moving); `detail` says why.

Accept found changes in the ship that are not committed; nothing was pushed or merged.
`files` names them. Unblocking checks again.

Accept found no commit on the ship's branch: there is nothing to open a pull request for
or to merge. Unblocking checks again.

The pull request's checks failed (pull-request mode); `checks` names the failed ones.
Unblocking pushes the ship again and watches the pull request again.
The pull request was closed on GitHub without merging.
The daemon restarted and the runner was gone.
The ship (worktree and branch) could not be prepared.

can_fast_forward.description: The base can be moved to the upstream without losing anything.

oneOf.description:
The runner has no directory to start in: the project has no repository, so the ticket has
no ship. Unblocking starts the ship and the runner again.

CardEdit.description: What the planner may change on a card that has not started.

design_first.description: Whether the agent shows a design for approval before any code.

designs.description: The card's designs, replacing the list (`[]` clears it); left out keeps them.

Chain.description:
A flow of tickets with dependencies and release milestones between them. Its status,
progress and "where it stopped" are computed from tickets and releases, never stored.

autostart.description: Start Ready tickets automatically (on by default).

oneOf.description: Overrides the project's review mode for every ticket that does not set its own.

reviewer.description: Overrides the project's reviewer profile for every ticket that does not set its own.

source.description:
The spec folder or chain file the chain was imported from, as an absolute path; `null`
for a chain made in Toknila or imported from pasted text.

ChainDeletion.description:
Answer of `DELETE /v1/chains/{chain}`: the chain and its cards are gone; what became of the
files around them. The repository folder and the `ship/*` branches stay.

project.description: Key of the project it belonged to.

tickets.description: How many cards went with it.

warnings.description: Cleanup that failed after the records were deleted. The deletion stands either way.

worktrees_removed.description: The ships' worktrees removed from the repository.

ChainDetail.description: A chain with its graph and computed status.

usage.description: Estimated token usage per card, by ticket key; cards that used none are absent.

warnings.description: What an import left out (a design the project does not have); only an import answers it.

ChainFile.description:
A chain file: body of `POST /v1/projects/{project}/import`, answer of
`GET /v1/chains/{chain}/export`.

ChainSettings.description:
What a person may set on a chain after it is made (a project takes the review fields in
[`crate::projects::PatchProject`]). A field left out is kept.

autostart.description:
Whether the chain starts its ready cards by itself. Turning it on starts the ready cards
that have a free slot, so it is a person's act; the planner cannot change a chain's graph
while it is on.

reviewer.description: Reviewer agent profile; an empty text goes back to `<worker profile>-reviewer`.

ChainStatus.description:
Computed chain status (never stored). Proposed wildcard cards are not part of the plan: they
do not count in `total` or `done`, but a pending decision makes the chain need a human.

ChainSummary.description: What a product person sees at a glance.

done.description: Merged, Released or Cancelled (Definition of Done: in the work branch), of `total`.

oneOf.description: When the last card of a finished chain was merged; none while the chain is not finished.

phase.description: Finished, active, waiting, idle or empty.

releasable.description:
Every card of the plan is in the work branch and one of them is not released yet: the
chain's end node offers Release.

total.description: Tickets in the plan: wildcard cards count only once approved.

Check.description: One line of the system check.

detail.description: What was found, in a sentence.

hint.description: What to do about it; always set, also when the check passes.

version.description: The version the tool reported, when it did.

CheckRun.description: One check of a pull request.

CheckState.description: How one check of a pull request stands.

CliLink.description:
`GET /v1/system/cli` and `POST /v1/system/cli/install`: the version of Toknila, the `tok`
command that ships next to the daemon and whether it is linked into `~/.local/bin`.

bundled.description: The `tok` binary next to the daemon, when there is one.

installed.description: The link exists and points at the bundled `tok`.

link.description: Where the link goes (`~/.local/bin/tok`), when the home folder is known.

on_path.description: The link's folder is on the daemon's `PATH`.

CommandPolicy.description: When the agent of a card wants to run a command.

Comment.description:
A permanent record in a ticket: an instruction from a person, an agent's report, or a decision.
Everything said to an agent is stored here first and delivered after.

oneOf.description: When the runner delivered it to the agent; `None` while pending.

CommentBody.description: Template fields of a comment. Empty fields are `None` and are omitted when rendered.

gist.description: One-line gist, the heading of the comment.

CommentKind.description: Comment type from the template; decisions later become ADRs.

DayUsage.description: One UTC day of the series.

trash_folder.description: Also move the repository folder to the system Trash. Without it the folder stays.

oneOf.description: The frame a `figma` design points at.

has_file.description: Whether a file is kept, served at `.../designs/{id}/file`.

hint.description:
What the person can do about a link without an image: export the frame, or why the fetch
failed. Never holds the token.

mime.description: Media type of the kept file; absent for a Figma link whose frame was not fetched.

size.description: Bytes of the kept file; zero without one.

thumb.description: Whether the file can be shown as a picture (everything kept but a pdf).

DesignId.description: Identifies a design of a project.

figma_token.description: Whether the project has a Figma token; the token itself is never sent.

DesignPick.description:
A design the planner names: its file name (or id) in the project's library, and the part of
the image that matters. The host finds the design and gives the use case a [`DesignRef`].

oneOf.description: In whole percent of the image; left out for the whole image.

DesignRef.description: A card's reference to a design of its project, with the part of the image that matters.

oneOf.description: `None`: the whole image.

Edge.description: Dependency edge: `to` cannot start before `from` is done.

ErrorBody.description: Error body of every failed request.

code.description: Stable machine code: not_found, bad_request, conflict, ambiguous, internal, unauthorized.

field.description:
The input the error belongs to (`repo_path`, `work_branch`, `default_profile`), when it
is about one field; a form shows the message next to that field.

EventRecord.description: One journal entry. `seq` is increasing; clients resume from it.

FigmaRef.description: The frame a Figma link points at.

url.description: The link as the person gave it.

FolderFate.description: What became of a deleted project's repository folder.

FolderNote.description: A subfolder that was not imported.

reason.description: Why: `no tasks.md`, or the error, which names the file and, for a `tasks.md`, the line.

FoundPlan.description: A plan found in a project's repository.

cards.description:
Cards an import would make (phases with tasks, or tickets); `null` when the file does not
parse.

imported.description: A chain of the project was imported from this path.

name.description: The folder's name, or the file's without `.toml`.

path.description:
Absolute path: what `POST /v1/projects/{project}/import-path` takes, and what a chain
imported from it records as its `source`.

HookWiring.description:
How an agent reports through hooks, a second event source: the runner writes a settings file
under the data home and passes its path with `settings_flag`.

enabled.description: Whether the launcher wires hooks into this agent.

settings_flag.description: Flag of the agent's command that takes the path of a generated hook settings file.

ImportPath.description: `POST /v1/projects/{project}/import-path`: what the daemon is to read and import.

path.description:
Absolute path of a TOML chain file, of a spec folder (one with `tasks.md`), or of a folder
whose subfolders are spec folders.

ImportPathResult.description:
Answer of `POST /v1/projects/{project}/import-path`. A chain file or a spec folder makes one
chain or fails as a whole (400 or 409, the message names the path); a folder of spec folders
imports each on its own and lists what it skipped and what failed.

failed.description: Spec folders that could not be imported; the others were.

chain.description: The new chain, as `POST /v1/projects/{project}/import` answers it.

done_cards.description: Cards imported as Merged because all their tasks were checked.

folder.description: The spec folder's or the chain file's name.

out_of_order.description: Done cards that sit behind a card with open tasks, one line each.

path.description: Where it was read from, absolute; the chain keeps it as its `source`.

allowed_actions.description:
What a person may do to the card now, as the state machine allows it; the window offers
no other card action.

answers.description:
How the question can be answered, as core allows it (`question` items; empty for an
`ask_human` question, which a comment answers).

detail.description:
The whole command of a permission request, when `text` carries only its summary (cut for
lists); absent otherwise.

done_cards.description: The cards done out of order that these subtasks are behind (`leftovers` items).

lines.description:
The last lines of the agent's screen, ANSI removed (`question` items of an agent that
waits on its screen).

link.description:
The card's pull request on GitHub, for a blocked card that has one (failed checks, a
closed pull request, a conflict); absent otherwise.

oneOf.description: Whose question it is (`question` items): the card's worker or its reviewer.

since.description: Since when it waits; items are sorted by this, newest first.

text.description: The question, the blocking reason, or the thread's title; empty otherwise.

thread.description: The thread's number on the card (`thread` items).

ticket.description: The card to open and act on; for `leftovers` the earlier card that holds the subtasks.

InboxKind.description: What kind of thing waits on the person; the order is the order clients group them in.

InstructionClaim.description:
Answer of `POST /v1/tickets/{ticket}/instructions/claim`: what a person told the agent while it
worked, now handed over and marked delivered.

count.description: How many instructions were handed over; 0 when nothing was pending.

reason.description: The instructions as one text for the agent, in the comment template; empty when none.

ItemBasis.description: How the reviewer came to its judgement of an item.

ItemOutcome.description: How one acceptance item stands, in the reviewer's eyes.

ItemVerdict.description: The reviewer's judgement of one acceptance item.

basis.description: Whether the reviewer ran what shows the item or only read; `read` when it says nothing.

item.description: The item's 1-based position in the ticket's acceptance list.

ListedProfile.description: A profile and where it comes from.

file.description: File name in the profiles folder; `None` for a built-in profile.

McpWiring.description:
How an agent receives its MCP server (the agent event contract): the runner writes a config
file under the data home and passes its path with `config_flag`.

config_flag.description: Flag of the agent's command that takes the path of a generated MCP config.

enabled.description: Whether the launcher wires the MCP server into this agent.

MergeMethod.description: How GitHub merges a pull request (`gh pr merge --merge|--squash|--rebase`).

MergeMode.description: Where an accepted card's work lands.

no_checks_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a pull request may have no check reported before a person is asked what to do.

pr_title.description: Title of a pull request; `{key}` and `{title}` are the card's.

MessageKind.description: Plain message, or a person's request for changes.

MoveInput.description:
`POST /v1/chains/{chain}/tickets/{ticket}/move`: put the card directly before or after
another card of the chain.

anchor.description: Ticket key of the card the moved card goes next to.

NewActivity.description: Body of `POST /v1/tickets/{ticket}/activity`: a sign of life from an agent's hook.

prompt.description:
A permission prompt notification: its message. The ticket's worker then waits for the
person; a reviewer's prompt is listed in the inbox.

session_id.description: Claude Code's session id, from the hook's input.

tool.description:
A `PreToolUse` hook: the summary of the tool call that is about to run (the command or the
file, at most 300 characters), kept to say what a later permission prompt is about.

transcript_path.description: The session's transcript file, from the hook's input.

NewAnswer.description: Body of `POST /v1/tickets/{ticket}/runner/answer`: a person's answer to what an agent asks.

always.description:
With `allow` on a worker's Bash prompt: also remember a rule for the command in the
project ("Allow always"), so later runs and prompts of running agents it covers are allowed
without asking. Ignored for any other answer or tool.

oneOf.description: Whose question: the ticket's `worker` (the default) or its `reviewer`.

text.description: The text of a `text` answer; the optional comment of a `deny`.

NewCard.description: What the planner gives for a new card.

after.description: Cards (keys) or release versions of the chain it waits for. Empty: the end of the chain.

design_first.description:
The card changes what the person sees: the agent shows a design for approval before any
code.

designs.description: Designs of the project the card is about, by file name or id.
